root_cause.text: The mpu3050 IIO driver registered the `iio_dev` in `mpu3050_common_probe()` before probe had finished initializing runtime PM, IRQ/trigger handling, and buffer state, exposing the device to userspace while its internal resources were not fully set up and creating a race condition.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `iio_device_register(indio_dev)` from an earlier point in probe, re-adds it at the very end "to prevent race conditions," and moves `iio_device_unregister(indio_dev)` to the start of remove; the new error path also cleans up PM, IRQ, and buffer setup done before registration, showing registration previously happened too early relative to those initializations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Defer or relocate IIO device registration in mpu3050_common_probe() by removing the early register-and-fail block.
intent_record.what: The call to iio_device_register(indio_dev) and its associated error handling block, including the dev_err() log and goto err_cleanup_buffer path, were removed from mpu3050_common_probe() before dev_set_drvdata(dev, indio_dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this probe path no longer registers the IIO device at that point in the function and will not fail or jump to buffer cleanup because of registration there, implying registration is deferred or handled elsewhere in the probe flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the IIO device during probe and properly unwind runtime PM, IRQ, and buffer resources if device registration fails.
intent_record.what: The change adds an explicit call to iio_device_register(indio_dev) before returning success, checks its return value, logs an error and jumps to a new err_iio_device_register label on failure, and expands the cleanup path at that label to restore runtime PM state with pm_runtime_get_sync(), pm_runtime_put_noidle(), and pm_runtime_disable(), optionally free the IRQ with free_irq(mpu3050->irq, mpu3050->trig) when irq is present, and then call iio_triggered_buffer_cleanup(indio_dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the probe function now actually registers the IIO device before succeeding, so the device becomes visible and usable only if registration completes successfully. If registration fails, the new error path unwinds previously initialized runtime PM, IRQ, and triggered buffer resources to avoid leaked state or partially initialized devices.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unregister the MPU3050 IIO device before cleanup and power-down so removal does not expose a partially torn-down device.
intent_record.what: The call to iio_device_unregister(indio_dev) was moved from the end of mpu3050_common_remove() to the beginning of the function, before the runtime PM calls, triggered buffer cleanup, IRQ free, and power-down logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the IIO device is now unregistered before its buffers, interrupt handling, and power state are torn down, preventing the device from remaining visible or accessible while its underlying resources are being dismantled during removal.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure the MPU3050 IIO device is correctly integrated into the IIO lifecycle by registering it during probe and unregistering it early during removal, with proper error unwinding to avoid exposing a partially initialized or torn-down device.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is early iio_dev registration in mpu3050_common_probe() before initialization completed. This change directly removes/defer that early registration block, addressing the race window exposed to userspace.

The changes directly concern when the IIO device is registered and unregistered relative to PM, IRQ, trigger, and buffer setup/teardown, which is the core of the race condition caused by exposing the device before initialization or during teardown was complete.

candidates.rationale: This is the core vulnerable action: the IIO device is registered too early in probe, exposing it to userspace before runtime PM, IRQ/trigger setup, and buffer initialization are fully completed.
This stores the device pointer immediately after early registration, making the partially initialized IIO device reachable through the driver data path while probe is still incomplete.

During remove, cleanup of buffer resources occurs before unregistering the IIO device, leaving the device still visible while internal resources are being torn down, reflecting the same lifecycle ordering flaw.
IRQ resources are freed before the IIO device is unregistered, so userspace can still access a device whose interrupt-backed internals are already dismantled.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the primary vulnerable statement. It registers the IIO device before probe has finished setting up runtime PM, IRQ/trigger handling, and buffered I/O state, exposing the device to userspace while initialization is still incomplete and creating the race condition described in the root cause.

Placed immediately after the early registration, this makes the partially initialized IIO device reachable through driver data while probe is still incomplete, reinforcing the premature exposure caused by early registration.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering is clearly present in `mpu3050_common_probe()`. The function calls `iio_triggered_buffer_setup(...)` and then registers the IIO device with `iio_device_register(indio_dev);` before probe has finished setting up trigger/IRQ support and runtime PM. Specifically, after `iio_device_register(indio_dev)` and `dev_set_drvdata(dev, indio_dev);`, the code only later does `if (irq) { ret = mpu3050_trigger_probe(indio_dev, irq); ... }` and then even later initializes runtime PM with `pm_runtime_get_noresume(dev);`, `pm_runtime_set_active(dev);`, `pm_runtime_enable(dev);`, `pm_runtime_set_autosuspend_delay(dev, 10000);`, `pm_runtime_use_autosuspend(dev);`, and `pm_runtime_put(dev);`. This matches the root cause: userspace can access the registered `iio_dev` before runtime PM and IRQ/trigger setup are complete, creating a race with partially initialized internal resources. There is no fix present that moves `iio_device_register()` to the end after trigger/runtime PM initialization or otherwise prevents early exposure.
